title: Burst: add cooldown/backoff + global circuit breaker with safe defaults
author: Keiko Yamamoto
description: Context: Dedicated Burst introduces a controlled shared burst pool. During early load tests/game-day we saw two failure modes: (1) rapid re-admission loops from retrying clients when burst is saturated, and (2) pool-level stress that should trigger a fast, deterministic stop of new burst admissions to protect neighbor SLOs and the hosted fleet. This PR implements per-tenant cooldown/backoff and a region/pool-scoped global circuit breaker for burst admissions, with config toggles and conservative defaults. Summary of changes: (a) Admission cooldown: when a tenant is denied burst for saturation/limit reasons, we apply a cooldown window before allowing another burst admission attempt for that tenant+region+pool (keyed by tenant_id, region, burst_pool_id). The cooldown is reason-aware and uses a capped exponential backoff (base 5s, factor 2.0, max 120s) with jitter to avoid synchronized thundering. (b) Global circuit breaker: when a burst pool crosses saturation gates (configured by a rolling window of reject rate and queue/latency signals) we open a circuit for that pool and deny new burst admissions with a stable reason code until the pool is healthy for a sustained close window. (c) Safe defaults: burst cooldown and circuit breaker are enabled by default for burst-enabled tenants; both can be toggled (and thresholds tuned) via control-plane config. Defaults are chosen to be conservative for pilot (deny faster, recover slower). (d) Observability hooks: emits structured deny reason codes and circuit breaker state transitions to logs/metrics, designed to integrate with ENG-4827 dashboards/alerts. (e) Routing behavior: when burst is denied due to cooldown or open circuit, routing follows existing fallback semantics (baseline -> compatible region/model fallback when allowed -> explicit deny). Notable semantics: cooldown only affects burst admission attempts (baseline capacity is unaffected) and does not change tenant hard caps; circuit breaker is pool-scoped and does not block other pools/regions. Testing: unit tests for backoff progression/jitter bounds, circuit open/close hysteresis, and deterministic keying; integration tests that simulate repeated retries and validate we stop hammering policy/routing when burst is saturated; added a small e2e harness stub to validate state propagation through routing context. Rollout: behind feature flags with default ON when burst is enabled; ops can override per-tenant and per-region quickly (see config fields below). Config (new fields): burst.guardrails.cooldown_enabled (bool, default true), burst.guardrails.cooldown_base_ms (default 5000), burst.guardrails.cooldown_max_ms (default 120000), burst.guardrails.cooldown_jitter_pct (default 0.15), burst.guardrails.circuit_breaker_enabled (bool, default true), burst.guardrails.cb_open_reject_rate (default 0.35 over 30s), burst.guardrails.cb_open_min_requests (default 200 over 30s), burst.guardrails.cb_close_healthy_window_s (default 120), burst.guardrails.cb_reason (enum -> maps to deny reason + header exposure rules). Follow-ups: ENG-4827 will add panels/alerts for cb_state and cooldown_denies; ENG-4824 may refine fallback behavior for certain deny reasons. Risk: This changes admission behavior only when bursting; designed to fail closed (deny burst) rather than risk neighbor impact. Includes guardrails to prevent unbounded memory growth in the cooldown state cache (LRU + TTL).

config: add burst.guardrails schema + defaults + validation
routing: wire cooldown/cb deny reasons into admission result + headers

snippet: Example deny behavior (pseudo): if cb.IsOpen(poolKey) { return Deny(BURST_DENY_CIRCUIT_OPEN, retry_after=cb.RetryAfter()) } if cooldownStore.InCooldown(tenantKey) { return Deny(BURST_DENY_COOLDOWN, retry_after=cooldownStore.RetryAfter(tenantKey)) } // otherwise evaluate limits + attempt admission; on deny, record cooldownStore.RecordDeny(tenantKey, reason)
review_conversation: Jordan Lee (review): The cooldown keying includes burst_pool_id; do we want it per region regardless of pool id? If we change pool topology later, a tenant might bypass cooldown by landing in a different pool label set.

Keiko Yamamoto (author): Good call. I started with pool_id to avoid penalizing other pools, but agree region-scoped is safer given pool discovery changes. Updated to key by tenant_id + region + gpu_class (derived) instead of pool_id. Tests updated.

Mina Haddad (review): For routing, please confirm that cooldown/circuit denials do not trigger region fallback loops. If baseline fails and burst is denied, we should not bounce across regions repeatedly.

Keiko Yamamoto (author): Yep. I added a routing guard: if deny_reason in {COOLDOWN, CIRCUIT_OPEN} we short-circuit additional burst attempts across regions in the same request path; we still allow baseline fallback per existing policy. Added integration test coverage.

Sean Gallagher (review): Circuit breaker thresholds: reject_rate 0.35 over 30s might open too late for small pools. Can we add min_requests gating + also allow opening on sustained queue time? Also need explicit log events for open/close transitions for postmortems.

Keiko Yamamoto (author): Added cb_open_min_requests (default 200/30s) and an alternate gate: if p95 admission queue wait > 250ms for 3 consecutive windows, open circuit. Transition events now emit structured logs (cb_open, cb_close) and a monotonic counter for transitions.

Rafael Mendes (review): Please add an operational override that can force-close the circuit breaker per pool for debugging (but gated behind admin config) and ensure state cache TTL is bounded so we don't leak keys during attacks.

Keiko Yamamoto (author): Added cb_force_state {AUTO,CLOSED,OPEN} with validation (admin-only). Cooldown and cb caches are LRU-bounded (10k keys default) + TTL (15m) + per-key last_access pruning. Documented in internal notes.
Ethan Park (review): Config defaults look reasonable. One nit: jitter_pct should cap at <=0.25 and base_ms must be >=1000. Add validation so we don't allow foot-guns.
Keiko Yamamoto (author): Done. Validation added + tests.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Sean Gallagher on 2025-07-12
release_notes: Internal: Burst guardrails now include cooldown/backoff on burst denial and a pool-scoped global circuit breaker to prevent retry storms and protect neighbor SLOs. Defaults enabled for burst-enabled tenants; configurable per tenant/region via control plane.
